The '''Ostzonenmeisterschaft 1948''' (English: Championship of the [[Soviet occupation zone|Eastern Zone]]) was the first football championship in what was to become [[East Germany]]. It was played in a one-leg knock-out format with ten participating teams. Each of the five [[States of Germany|''Länder'']]—[[Mecklenburg-Vorpommern]], [[Brandenburg]], [[Saxony]], [[Thuringia]] and [[Saxony-Anhalt]]—sent two representatives. The regional championships of Saxony, Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt were ended after the semi-finals as by then two participants had been determined. The Ostzone champion was supposed to take part in the [[German football championship 1948|1948 German championship]], playing [[1. FC Nürnberg]] in Stuttgart, but the team of [[FSV Zwickau|SG Planitz]] was not allowed to travel for political reasons.<ref name="Final-BZ">{{cite news|title=Planitz wurde Fußball-Ostzonenmeister|trans-title=Planitz became football champions of the Eastern Zone|volume=4|newspaper=[[Berliner Zeitung]]|issue=154|date=6 July 1948|page=4|language=German}}</ref><ref name="Final-ND">{{cite news|title=Planitz und Weißenfels-Mitte sind Ostzonenmeister|trans-title=Planitz and Weißenfels-Mitte are champions of the Eastern Zone|volume=3|newspaper=[[Neues Deutschland]]|issue=154|date=6 July 1948|page=4|language=German}}</ref>
